body: Overview An API key lets programs call the Tantra API on your behalf without a browser login. You use a key for scripts, integrations, and the Tantra MCP server. This article covers creating a key, copying it the one time it is shown, and revoking a key you no longer need. Keys are for headless access. If you only use Tantra in the browser, you do not need one. How it works You create a key on the API Keys page. Tantra generates a secret value that starts with tk live . The full value is shown to you once, at creation. Tantra stores only a hashed copy, so it can check a key you present later but can never display the original again. To use a key, your program sends it in the X-API-Key request header on every call to the Tantra API. Tantra looks up the key, confirms it is active and not expired, and treats the request as coming from your account. A key stays valid until it expires, if you set an expiry, or until you revoke it. Revoking is immediate. Before you start - You need to be signed in to Tantra in the browser to create a key. - Have a safe place to store the secret, such as a password manager or your integration's secret store. You cannot retrieve it later. Step-by-step: create a key 1. Open the API Keys page from the app navigation. 2. Click Create API Key . 3. Enter a Key Name . body: Overview The Tantra MCP server lets an AI client such as Claude or Cursor work with your Tantra account through tools. Once connected, you can ask the client to list campaigns, create contacts, or read dashboard metrics, and it calls Tantra for you. This article shows how to install the server, give it your API key, and confirm it works. MCP stands for Model Context Protocol, an open standard that lets AI clients call external tools. The Tantra MCP server is a thin proxy that forwards each tool call to the Tantra API. How it works The server runs as a small Node program. You start it, give it a Tantra API key, and point your AI client at it. When you ask the client to do something in Tantra, the client calls one of the server's tools, the server calls the Tantra API with your key, and the result comes back to the client. There are two ways to run the server: - Per user (stdio): you run the server locally for yourself. This is the common choice. Your API key lives in the server's environment. - Hosted (Streamable HTTP): one shared server serves many people, and each person sends their own key with each request. Use this only if you are hosting a shared server for a team. Most people want the per user setup. The rest of this article covers it. Before you start - A Tantra API key. Create one on the API Keys page and copy the tk live value at creation. See Create and manage API keys. - Node.js installed on your machine. - The Tantra MCP server files. title: Calendar campaign statuses explained
description: Understand every calendar campaign status in Tantra, from draft to completed, and why a campaign stays active for days.
headings: Why is my campaign Active for so long?

body: Overview Every calendar campaign shows a status badge. There are six values: Draft , Scheduled , Active , Paused , Completed , and Error . This article explains what each one means and how a campaign moves between them. One key idea makes the rest clear: for a running campaign, the status is worked out from the progress of its sending batches, not set by hand. As batches move from waiting to done, the status follows. How it works When you launch, Tantra splits your audience into batches that send over time. See How invitations are batched and sent. The status reflects where those batches stand: - If a batch is being sent right now, the campaign reads Active . - If every batch is done, it reads Completed . - If batches are still waiting to send, it stays Active because there is work left. - If a batch has failed, it reads Error . This is why a healthy campaign stays Active for days. It is not stuck. It is working through one batch every 24 hours until the list is finished. Active Running. It has sent some batches and has more to send, or is sending now. Paused You paused it. No further batches go out until you resume. Completed Every batch has been sent. title: How invitations are batched and sent
description: Tantra sends calendar invitations in batches over several days. Learn how batching works and why a campaign takes time to finish.
headings: Why does my campaign take days to send?
How many invitations go out per day per event?
What actually sends the invitation email?
Can I make it send faster?
Does closing the browser stop sending?
body: Overview Tantra does not send every calendar invitation at once. It adds your contacts to the event a batch at a time, spread over several days. This is deliberate. Adding a large group of attendees in one burst can trip Google's own limits and land invitations in spam. Batching keeps delivery steady and safe. This is the single most important thing to understand about calendar campaigns: a campaign with a large list takes days to finish sending, and that is by design. How it works When you launch, Tantra creates the calendar event first, with no attendees, so no invitation goes out yet. Then it builds a distribution plan, which is the queue of attendees waiting to be added. From there, invitations go out in batches: 1. Tantra adds a batch of up to 200 attendees to the event. 2. The moment attendees are added, Google emails them the invitation. 3. The next batch is scheduled for 24 hours later. 4. A background process checks every 5 minutes for batches that are due and sends them. So the pattern is one batch of up to 200 invitations, then a 24 hour wait, then the next batch, and so on until the list is done. Adding attendees is the exact step that triggers Google to send the invite. Within a single batch, Tantra adds attendees in smaller chunks of up to 50 per request, with a short pause of about 10 seconds between chunks, to stay within a safe sending rate for each mailbox. Where the first batch happens The first batch of each event is sent as soon as you start the campaign.

You see these counts on the Campaigns list, on each campaign's detail page, and, for webinar reporting, on the Reports page. How it works After invitations go out, Tantra checks each event's RSVPs on a schedule. Roughly every 10 minutes, a background process fetches the current attendee responses from Google, tallies them into accepted, declined, tentative, and no answer, and stores the result. To avoid redundant checks, an event that was refreshed very recently is skipped on the next cycle. Because this runs on a cycle, a response can take a few minutes to appear in Tantra after a prospect answers. The counts are near real time, not instant. title: What are calendar campaigns
description: Calendar campaigns reach prospects with Google Calendar invitations and track their RSVPs. Learn how the engine works and when to use it.
headings: How is a calendar campaign different from cold email?

body: Overview A calendar campaign reaches your prospects with a Google Calendar invitation instead of a plain email. Tantra creates a calendar event, then adds your contacts as attendees. Google sends each attendee the invitation. The message that lands in the prospect's inbox is a real calendar invite, so it shows up on their agenda. The engagement signal for a calendar campaign is the RSVP. You see who accepted, who declined, and who has not answered yet. This makes calendar campaigns a strong fit for webinars, live events, demos, and any offer where getting on someone's calendar is the goal. How it works Tantra sends from your own Google Workspace mailboxes. You connect a Google service account once and grant it domain-wide delegation, a permission you set in your Google admin console. Tantra then sends as your mailboxes using short-lived tokens. There is no personal password or sign-in. To set this up, see How Tantra sends as your mailboxes. When a calendar campaign runs, three things happen in order: 1. Tantra creates a Google Calendar event on a sender's calendar, with no attendees yet. 2. It adds your contacts to that event as attendees, a batch at a time. 3. The moment attendees are added, Google emails them the invitation. Adding attendees is what triggers the invitation email. title: Enrollment lifecycle and statuses
description: Understand how a contact moves through a Tantra cold email sequence, what each enrollment status means, and how to manage enrollments.
headings: How replies, bounces, and unsubscribes stop a sequence
body: Overview An enrollment is one contact's journey through a sequence. Each contact you add to a campaign gets one enrollment, which tracks their current step, their next send time, and their status. This article explains the statuses and how to manage enrollments from the campaign page. How it works When a campaign starts, Tantra creates an enrollment for each eligible contact and sets the first send time. A scheduler checks about once a minute for enrollments that are due, then hands each one to the send path. After a step sends, the enrollment advances to the next step and its next send time moves ahead by that step's delay. When the last step sends, the enrollment completes. Enrollments are de-duplicated by email address, so a contact who appears on two selected lists is enrolled once. Enrollment statuses An enrollment is always in one of these statuses: Status Meaning How it is reached --- --- --- active Moving through the sequence. Set at enrollment and after each step advances. paused Frozen. Not picked up by the scheduler. You pause the campaign, which freezes its active enrollments. completed Reached the end of the sequence or was stopped at the end. The last step sent, or you stopped it at the final step. replied The recipient replied, so the sequence stops. A reply is detected on the thread. bounced Delivery failed, so no more steps are sent. body: Overview Two things control how fast your cold email goes out: a sending window that defines when sending is allowed, and per-mailbox caps that limit how many emails each mailbox sends per day and per hour. Unlike calendar campaigns, these per-mailbox caps are enforced on every send. How it works Before every send, Tantra runs two checks: 1. Sending window. Is the current time inside the days and hours you allowed? If not, the step waits. 2. Quota. Does the mailbox have room under its daily and hourly caps? Tantra reserves a slot atomically, so two sends can never both take the last slot. Only when both pass does the email go out. A mailbox also waits at least half a second between sends, which keeps it under Gmail's per-mailbox rate. The sending window Set the window in Step 5 of the builder. - Timezone. The window is measured in the campaign timezone. The same timezone is also used if you schedule the campaign to launch later. - Days of the week. Toggle the days sending is allowed. At least one day is required. - Start hour and End hour. The hours sending is allowed, on the hour. The start hour must be before the end hour. Outside the window, due steps do not send. They wait and fire when the window next opens. This is true even if you chose Start now . Insert this image here. body: Overview The Email Analytics page shows cross-campaign performance for your cold email outreach. It answers three questions. How much are you sending? Who is engaging? Which campaigns and mailboxes perform best? Tantra measures engagement through clicks, replies, unsubscribes, and bounces. Tantra does not track opens. To learn why, read why Tantra does not track opens. Open the page from the sidebar. If you have no email campaigns yet, you see a No email campaigns yet card with a Launch a campaign button instead of the dashboard. How it works Every number on this page comes from real events in your sending and inbox pipeline. Nothing is sampled or estimated, with one exception noted below. - Sends are counted when a sequence step message actually leaves one of your connected mailboxes. Each successful send raises the campaign's sent counter by one. - Clicks come from click tracking. Only the first non-bot click per enrolled recipient raises the clicked counter. Automated scanner clicks are filtered out. - Replies and bounces come from reply detection. Tantra polls each sending mailbox, matches inbound messages to enrollments, and classifies each one as a genuine reply, a bounce, or an automatic response. - Unsubscribes are counted when a recipient confirms an unsubscribe. - Enrollments track each recipient's progress through your sequence. title: Warm up your sending mailboxes

headings: The warmed pool and the warm status
body: Overview Warmup gradually builds a mailbox's sending reputation before you use it for cold email at volume. Tantra warms a mailbox by sending a small, growing number of low-key emails between your own mailboxes and quietly marking them read. Mailboxes that send steadily and get engagement look trustworthy to inbox providers, which helps your real campaigns land in the inbox. How it works Warmup is peer-to-peer. A mailbox in warmup sends short, mundane emails to your other warmed mailboxes, which automatically mark them as read so they do not clutter those inboxes. The volume ramps up over time. - Starting volume: 5 emails per day. - Ramp: the daily volume rises by 5 every 3 days. - Target: it keeps climbing until it reaches the mailbox target, which defaults to 100 per day. Warmup needs a pool to send into. You need at least 2 warmed, connected, Gmail-capable mailboxes for warmup to do anything. With fewer, there is no peer to send to and warmup does nothing. Warmup traffic is counted separately from your campaigns. It does not consume a mailbox's daily or hourly campaign caps, so warming a mailbox never starves your real sends of quota. The warmed pool and the warm status On the Accounts page, each connected mailbox has a status you can set to Warmed or Cold , both on a single row and in the bulk update panel. body: Overview Cold email outreach is one of Tantra's two outreach engines. It sends multi-step email sequences from your own Gmail mailboxes, one step at a time, with a delay between steps. Each recipient moves through the sequence on their own schedule until they reply, unsubscribe, bounce, or finish every step. The other engine sends Google Calendar invitations. For a side-by-side comparison, see Calendar campaigns vs cold email. How it works A cold email campaign is a sequence of steps plus the audience, senders, and limits you attach to it. - A sequence is an ordered list of steps. Step 1 is sent first. Later steps wait a set number of days and can send as replies on the same email thread. - Senders are the Gmail-capable mailboxes you connected. Tantra sends as those mailboxes through a Google Workspace service account, so there is no separate password or per-mailbox sign-in. See How Tantra sends as your mailboxes. - An enrollment is one contact's journey through the sequence. Each contact you add becomes an enrollment with its own current step and next send time. - Limits control how fast you send. Each mailbox has a daily and hourly cap, and a sending window that defines the days and hours sending is allowed. Sending is not instant. A scheduler checks for due enrollments about once a minute, confirms the sending window is open, reserves quota on the mailbox, then sends the step. body: Overview Before a cold email campaign enrolls its contacts, Tantra runs a validation check on each recipient. Addresses that look risky or undeliverable are set aside in a quarantine so they are not emailed. This protects your sending reputation, since a bad list can hurt deliverability for every mailbox on your domain. How it works Validation runs when you launch a cold email campaign, after your suppression and unsubscribe lists have already been applied. Each remaining recipient goes through three checks in order. 1. Syntax check. The address must be a single line with one @ and no spaces, and the part after the @ must contain a dot. Anything else fails as invalid syntax. 2. Role-address check. Generic mailboxes that belong to a team rather than a person are flagged. These include local parts such as info , contact , sales , support , hello , admin , marketing , no-reply , noreply , postmaster , abuse , webmaster , billing , accounts , hr , jobs , and careers . 3. MX check. Tantra looks up the recipient domain to confirm it has mail servers. A domain with no mail records fails. A contact that fails any check is not enrolled. It is placed in quarantine with the reason recorded. Contacts that pass all three checks are enrolled and can receive email. body: Overview Click tracking tells you which recipients clicked a link in a cold email. Tantra measures engagement through clicks, replies, and unsubscribes. It does not use open tracking. To learn why, read why Tantra does not track opens. When click tracking is on, Tantra rewrites the links in your email so each click passes through a signed redirect first. The redirect records the click, filters out automated clicks from security scanners, and then sends the recipient on to the real page. This article explains how that works and where to see the results. How it works Click tracking runs in three stages. 1. Link rewriting at send time. When a step has click tracking enabled, Tantra rewrites each http and https link in the message body to point at a tracking redirect. Each rewritten link carries a signed token unique to that recipient and message. Links that are not web links, such as mailto: and tel: links, page anchors, and any link you mark to skip, are left untouched. 2. The signed redirect. When the recipient clicks, their browser hits Tantra's tracking redirect. Tantra verifies the token's signature, confirms the destination web address has not been altered, and confirms the destination uses http or https . If all checks pass, Tantra records the click and sends a 302 redirect to the original page. 3. Bot filtering. body: Overview A domain health report grades how well your sender domain is set up to reach the inbox. Every day, Tantra checks the domains behind your connected mailboxes for the three email authentication standards, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, plus whether your mail servers appear on public spam blocklists. Each domain gets a status of healthy, warning, or critical, and a score out of 100. These checks are read-only DNS lookups. Tantra never changes your DNS. It tells you what receivers see so you can fix problems before they cost you deliverability. What each check means - SPF lists which servers are allowed to send mail for your domain. Receivers use it to reject forgeries. A missing SPF record is a serious problem. - DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to your mail so receivers can confirm it was not altered in transit. - DMARC tells receivers what to do when SPF or DKIM fails, and where to send reports. A policy of quarantine or reject is stronger than a policy of none. - Blocklist check. Tantra resolves your mail servers to their addresses and checks them against major public spam blocklists. A listing badly hurts delivery. - MX records show which servers receive mail for your domain. Tantra reads them to run the other checks accurately. body: Overview One-click unsubscribe lets a recipient opt out of your emails in a single action, without opening a browser or filling in a form. It follows the mail industry standard, RFC 8058, that Gmail and Yahoo require from bulk senders. Tantra adds the required headers to your campaign emails and hosts a public confirmation page for the footer link. When a recipient opts out, they are added to your suppression list for that sender and stop receiving your emails. Honoring unsubscribes fast protects your sender reputation, which is why Tantra makes opting out effortless. How it works Tantra offers recipients two ways to opt out, and both end at the same place. - The mailbox unsubscribe button. On campaign emails, Tantra adds standard List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers. Gmail and Yahoo read these and show a native Unsubscribe link next to your sender name. When the recipient clicks it, their mail provider quietly tells Tantra to unsubscribe them. No page opens. - The footer link. Your email footer can carry an unsubscribe link. It opens a simple confirmation page with a Confirm unsubscribe button. Both paths add the recipient to your suppression list for that sender and mark their place in the sequence as unsubscribed, so no further steps are sent. Each unsubscribe link carries a signed token that identifies the recipient and sender. The link is single purpose and cannot be edited to unsubscribe someone else. body: Overview SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are three DNS records that prove your email is legitimately from your domain. Receiving mail servers check them on every message. When they pass, your cold email is far more likely to land in the inbox. When they are missing or misconfigured, your mail is more likely to hit spam or be rejected. Tantra sends your cold email through your own Google Workspace mailboxes using the Gmail API. That means the authentication records live in your domain's DNS, and you set them up once at your DNS provider. This article explains what each record does and how to publish it. Tantra does not change your DNS. It scans it daily and reports problems, which is covered in domain health reports. How the three records work together Each record proves a different thing about your mail. - SPF (Sender Policy Framework) lists which servers are allowed to send mail for your domain. A receiver looks up your SPF record and checks whether the sending server is on the list. Because Tantra sends through Google Workspace, your SPF record must authorize Google. - DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) adds a cryptographic signature to every message. The receiver uses a public key published in your DNS to confirm the message was signed by your domain and was not altered in transit. - DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) ties the two together. body: Overview Tantra does not track email opens, and this is a deliberate design choice. Most tools measure opens by embedding an invisible image, called a tracking pixel, in every email. Tantra never inserts one. Instead, Tantra measures real engagement through clicks, replies, and unsubscribes. This article explains the reasoning so you can trust the numbers you do see. Why open tracking is left out Open tracking sounds useful, but the way it works undermines the very outcome cold email needs, which is landing in the inbox. - Tracking pixels hurt deliverability. Spam filters recognize the hidden image that open trackers rely on. A remote image loaded from a tracking host is one of the signals filters use to sort promotional mail away from the inbox. Leaving the pixel out helps your mail read as a personal note. - Open numbers are unreliable. Many mail clients now pre-load images through privacy proxies. That records an open whether or not a human ever read the message, so the open rate is inflated and often meaningless. - A pixel makes your mail look like a marketing blast. Cold outreach works best when it reads as one person writing to another. A hidden tracker is exactly what a hand-typed message would not contain. - It respects the recipient. A pixel silently reports back the moment an email is viewed. Skipping it is a more honest relationship with the people you contact. title: Reply detection and intent classification
description: Learn how Tantra polls your mailboxes to detect replies, links them to the right campaign, and classifies each one with AI and a keyword fallback.
headings: Why is a reply not instant?
How does Tantra know a reply belongs to my campaign?

body: Overview When a prospect replies to one of your campaigns, Tantra detects the reply, links it to the right conversation, and works out what the prospect meant. This article explains the timing and the classification so the labels in your inbox make sense. It also explains why a reply is not instant. How it works Detection has two parts: finding the reply, then classifying it. Finding the reply Tantra checks your sending mailboxes on a repeating cycle. The check runs roughly every 30 seconds and picks up any mailbox that is due. How often a given mailbox is checked depends on how recently it last sent: When the mailbox last sent How often it is checked --- --- Within the last 3 days About every 30 seconds 3 to 14 days ago About every 2 minutes 14 to 30 days ago About every 10 minutes 30 to 90 days ago About every 30 minutes 90 or more days ago About every hour Never sent Not checked So a reply to a campaign you are actively running usually appears within a minute or so. A reply to an older campaign can take longer. When Tantra reads a new incoming message, it tries to match it to one of your outreach threads. It matches first by the conversation the message belongs to, and if that fails, it follows the reply's header trail back to a message you sent. If it cannot link the message to any of your outreach, the message is treated as not relevant and left out of the campaign inbox. headings: How intents appear in the inbox

body: Overview When a prospect sends a real reply, Tantra's classifier assigns it one of nine intents. The intent captures what the prospect meant, from clear interest to a request to be left alone. This article lists every intent and shows how it appears in your inbox. How it works Tantra reads the reply's subject and the first part of the body, then picks the single best-fitting intent along with a confidence score. When it is unsure, it prefers a catch-all rather than guessing. If the AI classifier cannot produce a result, Tantra keeps the tone guess from its keyword pass. For the detection and timing detail, see Reply detection and intent classification. The AI intent only overrides the keyword guess when the classifier is confident. Below that confidence, the reply keeps the keyword-based tone. The nine intents Intent What the prospect is signaling Inbox tone --- --- --- Interested Wants to talk, asks a question about your offer Positive Referral Points you to a colleague or names someone else to contact Positive Not interested Explicit disinterest, without asking to opt out Negative Objection, pricing Pushback specifically on price, budget, or cost Negative Objection, timing Interested but bad timing, such as "next quarter" Neutral Unsubscribe request Explicit opt-out, such as "remove me" or "stop" Negative Out of office An out-of-office auto-responder Neutral Auto response A generic auto-reply or ticket acknowledgement Neutral Other Anything that does not fit cleanly Neutral

body: Overview AI personalization rewrites your copy for each recipient using a text snapshot of that recipient's public website. Instead of one template that every prospect receives word for word, each person gets copy that references their own business. This article explains what personalization produces for each engine, how to turn it on, and what happens when it cannot run. Personalization is opt-in. It is off unless you enable it, and it always has a template to fall back to. How it works When personalization is enabled, Tantra fetches a text snapshot of the recipient's public website, then sends that snapshot and your template to an AI model. The model rewrites your copy so it fits that prospect while keeping your structure and any merge fields. See How website scraping feeds personalization for how the snapshot is gathered. The two engines produce different output. Cold email produces a personalized subject line and a personalized HTML body. Tantra runs the two as separate steps, first the subject, then the body, so each is shaped to its own rules. Your merge fields are preserved exactly. The result is one tailored email for that recipient. Calendar campaigns produce a personalized plain-text invitation description. This article covers creating, editing, and deleting them, plus the built-in AI helpers. How it works Each template belongs to your account and has one type, Calendar or Email . body: Overview Merge tags are placeholders that Tantra swaps for each recipient's own data when a message is sent. Spintax lets you offer several wordings and have Tantra pick one per recipient. Together they make one template read as many slightly different, personalized messages. This article explains the exact syntax and its rules. Every tag below is shown inside backticks so you can copy it. In your actual subject or body you type the tag itself. How it works Merge tags A merge tag is a field name wrapped in double curly braces, for example {{firstName}} . At send time Tantra replaces it with that recipient's value. You can reach nested data with dot paths, for example {{contact.company}} or {{sender.firstName}} . Dot paths resolve up to four levels deep. Anything deeper is treated as unknown. If a tag has no matching value, Tantra renders it as empty text. It does not print the raw {{tag}} and it does not error. A missing first name simply produces a blank, so write your copy so it still reads well when a value is empty. Spintax Spintax is a set of choices wrapped in single curly braces and separated by pipes, for example {Hi Hey Hello} . Tantra picks one option for each recipient. body: Overview To personalize a message, Tantra needs something to say about the recipient. It gets that by fetching a text snapshot of the recipient's public website. That snapshot is then given to the AI along with your template. This article explains where Tantra looks, when it skips a contact, and how the snapshot is used. Scraping only runs when you turn on AI personalization. If personalization is off, Tantra reads no websites. How it works When personalization runs for a contact, Tantra decides which website to read, fetches a text snapshot of that page, and passes the text to the AI. The snapshot is plain text, not a live browser session. Only a portion of the text is used in the AI prompt. Tantra uses up to the first 2000 characters, which is enough to capture what a company does without overwhelming the model. Tantra also reuses snapshots so it does not read the same site repeatedly. A site read for one contact can serve another contact on the same domain, which keeps campaigns fast. How Tantra chooses which site to read Tantra picks the target in this order. 1. If the contact has a website on record, Tantra uses that. 2. If not, Tantra derives one from the contact's business email domain. For example, a contact at jane@acme.com yields acme.com . 3. If the contact only has a personal webmail address, Tantra reads nothing for that contact. title: My calendar campaign is not sending invites
description: Fix a calendar campaign that is not sending invitations. Learn how daily batching, campaign status, and sender connection affect delivery.
body: Overview A calendar campaign reaches prospects through Google Calendar invitations. Tantra creates an event on your sender's calendar, then adds recipients as attendees in stages. Google sends the invitation email when each attendee is added. The most common reason a campaign "looks stuck" is not a fault. Invitations go out in daily batches, so a new campaign does not send to everyone at once. This article walks through that and the other real causes. Likely causes - The campaign is still sending in batches. Recipients are added in groups of up to 200 attendees, roughly 24 hours apart, so early batches send while later ones wait. - The campaign was never started. A campaign in draft does not send anything. - The campaign is scheduled for a future time and has not reached its start time yet. - The campaign is paused . - No connected sender is available, so Tantra cannot create or update the calendar event. - The event start time has nearly arrived, so Tantra stops adding new attendees. How batching works When you start a campaign, Tantra splits your contacts across your senders and stages them into batches. A background process checks for due batches every few minutes and sends the next batch when its scheduled time arrives. Standard batches are capped at 200 attendees and spaced about 24 hours apart. body: Overview When you launch a cold email campaign, Tantra validates each recipient before enrolling them. Addresses that fail validation are set aside instead of being enrolled. These are your quarantined contacts, and they appear on the campaign's Needs review tab. Quarantine protects your sending reputation. Sending to invalid or risky addresses causes bounces, which harm deliverability for every mailbox. This article explains the reasons and how to recover the affected contacts. Why contacts are quarantined At launch, after removing anyone on your unsubscribe or suppression lists, Tantra checks every remaining recipient for three things: - Valid email shape. A malformed address, with spaces, a missing domain, or more than one at-sign, is rejected. - Not a role address. Shared inboxes such as info@, sales@, and no-reply@ are set aside because they rarely belong to a single person. - A domain that can receive mail. Tantra looks up the domain's mail records. If the domain has no mail exchange record, it cannot receive email and is set aside. Contacts that fail any check are not enrolled. Everyone who passes is enrolled and starts the sequence. title: My emails are not sending
description: Fix a cold email sequence that is not sending. Check daily and hourly limits, sending windows, sender status, suppression, and enrollment state.
body: Overview A cold email sequence sends from your connected mailboxes, one step at a time, on a schedule. Several safety limits sit between an enrolled contact and an actual send. When a send is held back, the contact is not lost. Tantra simply reschedules it for later today, tomorrow, or the next open sending window. This article covers why a sequence pauses itself and how to confirm it is working. Likely causes - The sender hit its daily limit, so remaining sends move to tomorrow. - The sender hit its hourly limit, so sends move forward about an hour. - The current time is outside the campaign's sending window. - The campaign is paused or archived, so no steps run. - The enrollment is paused , or already reached a final state like replied , bounced , or unsubscribed . - The recipient is on a suppression or unsubscribe list, so the send is skipped. - The sender shows Disconnected , so Tantra cannot authenticate to send. How limits and windows work Each sender has a per-day and per-hour send limit. The defaults are 50 sends per day and 25 per hour, and you can lower them per sender on the Accounts page. When a sender reaches its daily limit, the next step for that contact is rescheduled for the following day. When it reaches its hourly limit, the step is pushed forward about an hour so the new hour can start fresh. title: AI personalization is not working
description: Fix AI personalization when recipients get generic copy. Check that AI mode is on, the website is reachable, and an LLM provider is available.
body: Overview AI personalization rewrites your copy for each recipient using a snapshot of the recipient's public website. When it cannot run, Tantra does not fail the send. It quietly falls back to your plain template so the message still goes out. That is why the usual symptom is not a missing email. It is recipients receiving generic, template copy instead of tailored copy. This article explains why the fallback happens and how to get personalization running. How personalization decides to run For each recipient, Tantra checks a short list before calling the AI. If any check fails, it uses your template instead: 1. The step or event must have AI personalization turned on. It is off by default. 2. The recipient must have a business domain. Personal webmail addresses such as gmail.com, yahoo.com, hotmail.com, outlook.com, icloud.com, and protonmail.com are skipped. 3. A website must be resolvable, either from the contact's website field or from the email domain. 4. The website must return usable content when Tantra fetches it. 5. An AI provider must be available to generate the copy. Only the recipient's public website content feeds the AI, and only the first portion of that page is used in the prompt. title: A sender shows as disconnected
description: Fix a sender that shows as disconnected. Check domain-wide delegation, Gmail and Calendar scopes, and re-verify the mailbox against your service account.
body: Overview Tantra sends as your mailboxes using a Google service account with domain-wide delegation. The service account borrows the identity of each mailbox using short-lived tokens. It never uses a password. A sender shows Disconnected when none of your uploaded service accounts can borrow that mailbox's identity. This almost always means a delegation or scope gap in your Google Workspace admin console, or that the service account was removed. This article shows how to confirm and fix it. How connection is checked When you add senders, Tantra tries to impersonate each mailbox with every service account you have uploaded. If one succeeds, the sender is linked to that service account and the badge turns to Connected . If none succeed, the badge stays Disconnected and a short reason appears on the row. There is a second, separate check for Gmail. A service account can be authorized for Calendar but not Gmail. In that case the sender shows Connected with a Calendar-only badge instead of Gmail capable . Calendar-only senders can send calendar invitations but cannot send cold email. Likely causes - Domain-wide delegation was never granted for the service account's client ID. - The delegation grant is missing one or more required scopes. - The service account was deleted or disabled in Google Cloud, or removed from Tantra. - The mailbox address is misspelled or belongs to a different domain than the delegation grant. - Delegation was granted moments ago and has not fully propagated
